target_customer: Developers and websites adding two-factor authentication, plus end users of the Authy app
problem: Few sites supported two-factor authentication because building it was hard for developers.
business_model: Usage-based API charged per authentication, plus a free consumer authenticator app

competitors.name: Google two-step verification
competitors.what: Free two-step authentication for Google accounts and developers

technical_complexity.rationale: Reliable SMS, voice and token delivery plus cryptography and an API for developers, with uptime as the hard part.

defensibility.rationale: Integration into developer apps created some switching cost, but the core was copyable and Google offered free alternatives.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Twilio, which delivered Authy's SMS codes, acquired Authy in February 2015 at an undisclosed price.

market_need_then: Account takeovers such as the Dropbox incident in 2012 raised interest in two-factor, but few sites supported it, and Authy said it began with fewer than 100 users.

branding.domain_note: Uses authy.com, now a Twilio Authy page.

identity.logo: Security style mark in red, silver and white per a third party logo site

branding.brand_signature: Free multi-device authenticator app with cloud backup

rebrands.why: Twilio added its ownership name five years after the acquisition, per Twilio and Android Police.

branding.community_and_virality: Used by Coinbase, Cloudflare, Humble Bundle and Twitch per the company description. Consumer app widely adopted.

brand_strength.rationale: A recognized authenticator app with a strong user base, kept as a brand by Twilio after the acquisition and still promoted in 2026.

outcome_analysis: Authy turned two-factor authentication into an API and a consumer app, raised a roughly 750 thousand dollar seed in 2012 and a larger angel seed announced September 2014, then was acquired by Twilio in February 2015. The price was not disclosed. The app remains active under Twilio Authy, so the outcome was a strategic acquisition of a product with real adoption.
notes: TechCrunch in September 2014 reported 2.3 million dollars of seed in total including the 750 thousand dollar first seed, so the 2014 round amount is left null to avoid double counting. Totals vary by tracker (3.0 to 3.8 million dollars). Dealroom lists about 6.1 million dollars for the acquisition, unverified. Another source names Antonio Garcia as a founder, not on the YC page, so not listed. Duo Security and others not confirmed as 2012 competitors.
